approved: Commonwealth Electoral Amendment (Political Donations and Other Measures) Bill 2016
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would lower the threshold for disclosing political donations from over $10,000 to $1,000 and ban foreign donations.
It would require donors and recipients to file returns within 8 weeks after polling day and twice yearly, and treat related parties as one entity for the disclosure threshold.
The bill would also ban anonymous gifts over $50 and introduce new offences and higher penalties for breaches.
Reduces the disclosure threshold from more than $10,000 to $1,000.
Requires returns within 8 weeks of polling day for election-period gifts.
Requires biannual returns within 8 weeks after 31 December and 30 June.
Prevents donation splitting by treating related political parties as one entity.
Makes it unlawful to receive gifts of foreign property for parties, candidates, and some entities.
Extends the ban on anonymous gifts to all except those of $50 or less at public activities or private events.
Political parties, candidates, members of Senate groups, associated entities, and people incurring political expenditure.
